solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shell makes vehicle fast

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
apace means quickly, fast

explanation.surface: A shell turns a vehicle speedy, as if armour plating were a turbo.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard protective upper covering of a crab, turtle or beetle: a synonym for its shell.

clue.text: Metal used in synchromesh

indicators.note: the letters are used in, contained within, the longer word that follows

explanation.surface: A remark on which metal goes into a car's synchromesh gearbox.
explanation.walkthrough: Synchromesh is the gearbox mechanism that lets gears mesh smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrome is the everyday name for chromium, a hard shiny metal used in plating.

clue.text: Ruling about well-bred chap

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a gent is a gentleman, a well-bred man

explanation.surface: A judgment concerning some refined gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruling' looks like a noun, a verdict; it is an adjective, as in 'Prince Regent'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective placed after a title, regent means governing in place of a monarch, so ruling.

clue.text: Clean up English decorations

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written bottom to top, turned round

parts.note: to mop is to clean
Poms is Australian slang for English people

explanation.surface: An instruction to tidy away the English bunting after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' signals a turnaround in this down light. 'English' is Australian and New Zealand slang for the English, a usage solvers outside those countries may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompoms are woolly balls used as ornaments on hats and costumes, so a kind of decoration.

clue.text: Near ancient? — He's not exactly that!

definitions.text: Near ancient? — He's not exactly that!

indicators.note: the words are not given exactly as printed but in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A teasing remark about someone very old who is not quite ancient yet.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a person aged a hundred is near ancient, yet not exactly ancient.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has reached a hundred years of age is very old, close to what one might jokingly call ancient.

clue.text: Cab takes German round motorway

parts.note: Hans is a typical German man's name
O is round in shape
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A taxi picks up a German driver on the ring road.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain motorways are numbered with M, as in M25.
explanation.definitionFit: A hansom was a two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage for hire, the Victorian taxi.

clue.text: Hospital worker — nut mostly employed by emergency room

indicators.note: mostly means the word lacks its final letter

parts.note: an almond is a nut

explanation.surface: A hospital employee, a bit nutty, is taken on by casualty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of ALMOND to leave ALMON.
explanation.definitionFit: An almoner was a hospital social worker in Britain, looking after patients' welfare.

clue.text: Surveillance operation officers finally given fast food

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: takeout is food bought ready to eat, fast food

explanation.surface: Police officers on a watch are eventually given a burger to keep them going.
explanation.definitionFit: A stakeout is a period of secret watching of a place by police, a surveillance operation.

clue.text: A daughter's in jolly pickle

indicators.note: in means the letters go inside another word

parts.note: a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine

explanation.surface: A daughter is in a jolly fine mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective and 'pickle' like a fix; a jolly is naval slang for a marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A marinade is a seasoned liquid in which food soaks before cooking, a kind of pickle.

clue.text: Closely control, metering supply

indicators.note: supply read as an adverb, suppl-y meaning supplely, flexibly, so the letters bend into new order

explanation.surface: Advice on tightly regulating how much of a utility is measured out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is read as 'supplely', bendily, an anagram sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To regiment is to organise people or things strictly, imposing tight control.

clue.text: Mischievous creature bearing damage

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous sprite
air means manner or bearing

explanation.surface: An imp's attitude causes harm.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair is to weaken or harm, so to damage.

clue.text: Access point for tunneller round a new hospital

indicators.note: round means the first word goes around the others

parts.note: a mole is an animal that tunnels
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A digger's way in near a recently built hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A manhole is a covered opening giving workers entry to a sewer or underground service: an access point.

clue.text: Colonist losing head with Northern light

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a planter was an early settler in a colony

explanation.surface: A settler, beheaded, alongside the northern lights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops the P of PLANTER, leaving LANTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable case holding a lamp or candle, a light.

clue.text: Dreadfully ill advocate self-indulgent lifestyle

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests the letters are badly mangled, out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A sickly lawyer argues for a life of pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: La dolce vita, Italian for the sweet life, means a life of luxury and self-indulgence.

clue.text: Remain idle and get drinks for everyone

definitions.meaning: to buy a round of drinks, splitting the phrase as ...

explanation.walkthrough: In a British pub, to stand a round is to pay for everyone's drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To loaf about idly is one sense; read as two words it also means treating the whole group at the bar.

clue.text: Cover for weapon to defy strike without least bit of damage

parts.note: to scab is to work as a strike-breaker
bar means except, without

indicators.note: least bit of means only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Something protecting a weapon so it can resist a blow undamaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like an instruction to remove; here it is BAR, meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is a sheath that holds a sword or dagger, a cover for a blade.

clue.text: Ordinary colours

definitions.meaning: a military flag or banner, the regimental colours

explanation.definitionFit: The word means normal or usual, and also a flag carried as an emblem, like regimental colours.

clue.text: Recall a trip possibly made by one on mushroom in fantasy

indicators.note: possibly says the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Remembering a hallucinogenic trip, perhaps on magic mushrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: In Alice's Adventures in Wonderland a hookah-smoking creature sits on a mushroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's story has a hookah-smoking larva perched on a mushroom, an example from that fantasy.

clue.text: Crash into servant in storm

parts.note: to ram is to crash into
a page is a young servant

explanation.surface: A vehicle smashes into a servant during a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' is a verb here: to rampage is to storm about.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about violently, to storm around.

clue.text: Salesman gets extra pay to perform again

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
a rise is a pay increase

explanation.surface: A salesman wins a pay increase.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprise is to repeat a song or role, to perform it again.

clue.text: Shrivel up moving right forward, and feel embarrassment

indicators.note: moving says one letter changes its place in the word
forward says the letter shifts towards the front

parts.note: to wither is to shrivel

explanation.surface: Someone shrinks with mortification as they shuffle to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving ... forward' shifts the R of WITHER from the end up to second place.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to squirm, as with acute discomfort or shame.

clue.text: Doctor upset politician — it can cause serious damage

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A medic upsets a politician, causing real harm.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a fungus that decays timber, causing severe structural harm to buildings.

clue.text: Slave such as Connery, Moore…

definitions.meaning: Sean Connery and Roger Moore each played James Bond

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a serf bound to service; split in two it describes actors who played 007.

clue.text: Supreme leader for each in regressive ancient city

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other
regressive means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: Rome is the ancient city
per means for each

explanation.surface: A head of state in a city going backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regressive' turns the city round to EMOR, which is then opened up to take the Latin-derived word for each.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the sovereign ruler of an empire, its supreme head.

clue.text: Popular film in which girl meets sailor

parts.note: Ava is a girl's name
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A romantic film where a girl meets a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: James Cameron's Avatar was one of the highest-grossing films ever, so a popular film.

clue.text: Clergyman — one in great church

indicators.note: in means one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: a minster is a large important church, like York Minster
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A priest working in a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is a member of the clergy, especially in Protestant churches.

clue.text: Comedian with sign of hesitation to move uncertainly

parts.note: Ken Dodd was a famous British comedian
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A comic hesitates before shuffling unsteadily.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Dodd was a long-running Liverpool comedian known for tickling sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodder is to totter or walk shakily, moving without certainty.

clue.text: A sneak initially enters secure window

indicators.note: enters means the letters go into another word

parts.note: to cement is to secure, fix firmly

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A thief first gets in through a fastened window.
explanation.definitionFit: A casement is a window hinged at the side, opening like a door.
